content.name: Xenon Pressure
content.description:
The Xenon are held back by a handful of numbers. Their faction logic wants exactly seven shipyards and seven wharfs (four without the Split and Terran DLC), rolls a five percent chance every minute or two to start a missing one, their jobs cap how many N, M, P, K and I are ever in the galaxy at once, their ships cost about twice what the galaxy can feed them, and their miners carry 9 500 units and turn on whatever shoots them.
This mod puts the live numbers on sliders - station targets, a ratio of stations to sectors held, how big an invasion fleet gets and how much of it may be newly built, how many groups go after stations in contested space, and whether they raid beyond their borders - makes the miners' reaction to an attack a setting, and ships tuned quotas, cheaper hulls and a bigger hold as static patches. It replaces Xenon Hell and AI Xenon Miners; disable both.
[h2]Settings[/h2] [list] [*][b]Sectors per shipyard[/b] and [b]Sectors per wharf[/b] - 0 to 5, default 0. How many shipyards and wharfs the Xenon faction logic wants to own, as one per this many sectors they own or contest, rounded up: at 5 one per five sectors, at 1 one in every sector. 0 leaves the vanilla target, which is 4, plus 2 with Split Vendetta and 1 with Cradle of Humanity. Missing ones are built where the Xenon already hold space, one per sector. [*][b]Constructions in progress[/b] - 0 to 10, default 0 (no limit). How many shipyards and wharfs may be under construction at once before another is started, so their miners feed a few sites instead of forty. [*][b]Build chance[/b] - 1 to 100 percent, vanilla 5. The chance, per 1-2 minute evaluation, that a missing shipyard or wharf is started. At 5 a replacement takes 20-40 minutes on average to begin; at 100 it starts on the next cycle. [*][b]Invasion fleet size[/b] - 50 to 300 percent, vanilla 100. Scales the strength a Xenon invasion gathers before it moves and the ceiling it may request up to. An invasion that cannot reach its strength within an hour gives up, so pair a high value with a high build share. [*][b]Invasion build share[/b] - 0 to 100 percent, vanilla 25. How much of each invasion group may be newly built rather than pulled off patrol. New ships still count against the job quotas. [*][b]Station attack groups[/b] - 1 to 6, vanilla 2. How many groups may be attacking enemy stations in a Xenon or contested sector at once. [*][b]Long range raids[/b] - on or off, vanilla off. Lets the Xenon send expeditions against sectors of every faction, not only gate neighbours. At most two at a time; they gather for two hours, stay an hour, build nothing and come home. [*][b]Miner behaviour[/b] - 0, 1 or 2, default 2. What a Xenon miner or energy hauler does when shot at: 0 is vanilla and it turns to fight, 1 keeps flying and neither fights nor flees, 2 always flees at once and does not drop laser towers on the way out. [*][b]Debug logging[/b] - off by default. Writes what the mod does to the debug log; needs the game started with -debug scripts. [/list] Changes take effect on the next evaluation and the next attack, with no reload. The Xenon are already at the highest aggression mood the game has, which is why there is no mood slider: these are the numbers that mood feeds.
[h2]Static changes[/h2] [list] [*]Xenon M miner cargo 9 500 to 22 500. [*]Xenon job quotas raised: about twice the miners and energy haulers, five carriers on the border, 21 destroyers on cluster patrol, more fighters, scouts, deep-space wings and escorts. Every galaxy quota stays below its maxgalaxy so the job engine does not spawn and cull in a loop. [*]Xenon ship build resources halved for the N, M, P, K, I and both miners. [*]Xenon station module resources and build times halved; the modules they share with the Commonwealth only in their Xenon recipe. [/list] These are library and macro patches, read when the game starts; they cannot be sliders. They take effect on the next load, and quotas fill as the job engine spawns ships.
[h2]Where to change them[/h2] With SirNukes Mod Support APIs installed: [b]Options - Extension Options - Xenon Pressure[/b].
Without that API the mod runs off the constants at the top of md/drjele_xenon_pressure.xml, re-read on every savegame load - editing one and reloading is enough. Any other mod or cheat menu can also override them at runtime through the globals $DrJeleXenonSectorsPerShipyard, $DrJeleXenonSectorsPerWharf, $DrJeleXenonMaxConstructions, $DrJeleXenonBuildChance, $DrJeleXenonFleetSize, $DrJeleXenonBuildShare, $DrJeleXenonStationAttackGroups, $DrJeleXenonLongRangeRaids and $DrJeleXenonMinerBehaviour. The cargo, quotas and resources are edited in the patch files under libraries/ and assets/.
[h2]Where the defaults are not vanilla[/h2] Miner behaviour defaults to 2 (flee, no laser towers), and the cargo, quota and resource patches are always on. Every other setting defaults to vanilla.
[h2]Dependencies[/h2] [list] [*][b]X4: Foundations 9.00[/b] - required. [*][b]SirNukes Mod Support APIs[/b] - optional, and only for the in-game options menu. Everything works without it. [*]No DLC required. [/list]
[h2]Notes[/h2] Works on an existing savegame. The station targets, invasion numbers and the miner reaction are read by the vanilla scripts at the moment they evaluate, through small patches whose selectors each match exactly one node, so nothing has to be applied to a game already in progress. Long range raids is the one manager variable, written on every load.
Incompatible with Xenon Hell and AI Xenon Miners: all three patch the same nodes of aiscripts/interrupt.attacked.xml, and Xenon Hell also replaces the job quotas and ship wares this mod patches.
Removing it: turn Long range raids off and save before removing the mod; otherwise the expedition enemy list remains in the savegame. Stations already built stay, ships already spawned stay until the job engine trims them to the vanilla quota, and the miners' hold shrinks back to 9 500 on the next load. Slider values persist in the options API's own storage.
Source and full documentation: https://github.com/drjele/x4-xenon-pressure

text.name: Xenon Pressure
text.description: Sliders for how many shipyards and wharfs the Xenon want per sector they hold, how big their invasion fleets get and how much of them they build new, how many groups attack stations in their space, whether they raid beyond their borders, a setting for what their miners do when attacked, and static patches for miner cargo, job quotas and ship build costs. Replaces Xenon Hell and AI Xenon Miners. Works on an existing savegame.
